description: A PHP static analysis tool for finding errors and security vulnerabilities in PHP applications

latest_release.name: 7.16.0 Star projection
latest_release.body:
## Features

- **Star projection `Foo<*>`**: Kotlin's syntax for a generic argument you don't know. Reads go through the template's bound (`Box<*>::get()` is `object` for `T of object`), writes through it expect `never`, and `Box<*>` accepts any `Box`. See [Star projection](https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/blob/7.16.0/docs/annotating_code/templated_annotations.md#star-projection). (#13139, #13493, #14619, #14598, @alies-dev)

## Performance

- Scan workers send back only the stubs they added: −9 % wall, −14 % memory on a large Laravel app (8 threads, no cache). (#12558, @alies-dev)
- Usage-inferred parameter types are recorded only for methods in the project directories: −8 to −15 % wall on apps that analyse their tests (one thread). (#13901, @alies-dev)
- No exponential clause growth in `||` chains of `str_starts_with()`. Important for WordPress projects (#14653, @alies-dev)
- Config loading skips directories a `**` entry already matched: 60 to 85 % faster with `**/vendor`-style entries. (#14624, @alies-dev)
- A class docblock is split into lines once for all its `@method` tags: scanning up to 5 % faster on classes with hundreds of them, such as AWS SDK clients and Laravel Facades. (#14620, @alies-dev)

## Fixes

### Templates

- An inherited property or callable resolves the parent's template through what the child passes to it (`@extends Base<list<U>>`, `@extends Base<Box<TModel>>`, also across two `@extends` levels). (#14487 @jirkace, #14558 @alies-dev)
- Callables of a non-generic child of a generic class bind the parent's template. (#14578, @alies-dev)
- `new` on a `@template-covariant` class infers `never` for a template nothing can constrain, so `new Coll()` fits `Coll<int>`. (#14449, @jirkace)

### Callables and invokable objects

- An intersection whose later member has `__invoke` is callable. (#14610, @alies-dev)
- `array_map()` with an invokable object as the callback infers the return type of `__invoke` instead of `list<mixed>`. (#14654, @alies-dev)
- An invokable object, a function name or an array passed where a `Closure` is expected is an `ArgumentTypeCoercion`, not an `InvalidArgument`. (#14657, @alies-dev)

### Other

- `--find-references-to` finds the calls of a function. (#14648, @jirkace)
- A crashing worker says which file it was processing. (#14651, @jirkace)
- A failing worker pool task (e.g. a plugin hook throwing in a scan worker) is reported once, not again as an unhandled future. (#14595, @alies-dev)

## Docs

- Docs examples are self-contained and declare the config they need. (#14585, @danog)

## Internal changes

- CI: Shared duplicated code and dropped dead code. (#14553, @orklah)
- CI: Perf bot: issues changed in place are shown as diffs, a regression warns at +10 % wall per project and +5 % in total, WordPress joins the corpus, and PRs that touch only tests or CI are skipped. (#14568, #14575, #14655, #14656, @alies-dev)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/compare/7.15.0...7.16.0

detail.readme:
Psalm

[![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/dt/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm coverage](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/coverage.svg?)](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm level](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/level.svg?)](https://psalm.dev/) Psalm is a static analysis tool for finding errors in PHP applications. [Join the official Psalm news channel](https://t.me/psalmphp) and the Psalm community on [Telegram](https://t.me/psalmphp_community) and [Discord](https://discord.gg/RwH8rEpxt9)! ## Installation To get started, check out the [installation guide](docs/running_psalm/installation.md). ## Live Demo You can play around with Psalm [on its website](https://psalm.dev/). ## Documentation Documentation is available on [Psalm’s website](https://psalm.dev/docs), generated from the [docs](https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/blob/master/docs) folder. ## Support Psalm development You can support Psalm development by requesting a support contract from [Daniil Gentili](https://daniil.it), the only active maintainer of Psalm. Support contracts can cover full integration of Psalm into existing codebases, support for Psalm issues and development of additional Psalm features. See [here »](https://daniil.it) for info, pricing and contact information. ## Interested in contributing? Have a look at [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Who made this Built by Matt Brown ([@muglug](https://github.com/muglug)). Maintained by Daniil Gentili ([@danog](https://github.com/danog)), Alies Lapatsin ([@alies-dev](https://github.com/alies-dev)) and Orklah ([@orklah](https://github.com/orklah)). Former maintainer: Bruce Weirdan ([@weirdan](https://github.com/weirdan)). The engineering team at [Vimeo](https://github.com/vimeo) have provided a lot encouragement, especially [@nbeliard](https://github.com/nbeliard), [@erunion](https://github.com/erunion) and [@nickyr](https://github.com/nickyr).
